html:
The Janos were an Indigenous people of the dry basin of northwest Chihuahua, Mexico, around the town and river that keep their name, near the border with New Mexico. They lived by hunting and gathering and moved with the seasons, together with allies such as the Jocome, Suma and Jumano.

Spanish settlers and missions reached the area in the late 1600s, and the Janos joined risings against Spanish rule in 1684. Around 1690 Spain built the presidio of Janos, a fort that guarded the frontier for over a century. The Janos and Jocome merged into the Chiricahua Apache in the 1700s, and the presidio became a place where Apache bands made peace and received rations. See also the Manso.
